slides.texte_overlay:
How to become a natural
at casual conversation
Treat every chat like a short game of catch. They throw, you catch and throw back. Answer, then add one question. Conversations flow when nobody holds the ball too long.
Notice what people are carrying or wearing. A book, a band shirt, a sports bag. "Do you climb?" is an easy, natural opener that shows you pay attention.
Use "me too" moments. When you share something in common, say it. "No way, I grew up near there too." Shared ground turns strangers into friends quickly.
Don't plan your next line while they talk. Just listen. Your next question will come naturally from what they say, and it'll sound real instead of rehearsed.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Casual conversation is easy when your head is full of small, fun things to share.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Casual talk is easy with a head full of fun things.

slides.texte_overlay: Let it be light. Not every chat needs depth. Laughing about the weather or the queue is a perfectly good conversation, and people enjoy easy moments.
End before it fades. "Great talking, enjoy the rest of your day." Leaving while it's still pleasant makes people happy to talk to you again next time.
